study_name.evidence_quote: Adrian Tett, Kun D. Huang, Francesco Asnicar... The Prevotella copri Complex Comprises Four Distinct Clades
study_name.notes: Study name constructed from lead author and main research focus, as no explicit study identifier provided

zigosity.notes: No twin zygosity information reported in the paper.

age_min.evidence_quote: For Ethiopia 50 individuals (24 adults...26 infants, avg age (yrs): 1.31 (s.d.1.05), range 0.167-4.5 yrs).
age_min.notes: Minimum age from Ethiopian cohort infants (0.167 years = ~2 months). Study includes multiple cohorts with different age ranges.

age_max.evidence_quote: And for Tanzania 68 individuals (37 adults, avg age (yrs): 29.27 (s.d. 8.88), range: 18-61, sex: 48.65% female, 51.35% male
age_max.notes: Maximum age from Tanzanian cohort adults (61 years). Study includes multiple cohorts with different age ranges.

age_years.notes: Study reports mean ages and ranges by cohort but not a single overall age_years value for all participants.

antibiotics_current_use.notes: Antibiotic use not reported in the paper.

bmi.notes: BMI mentioned as a factor considered (Table S1) but no specific BMI values reported in main text.

dietary_restriction.notes: Dietary patterns described for populations (e.g., traditional diets high in fiber) but no individual dietary restrictions reported.

disease.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
disease.notes: All newly sequenced cohorts (Ghana, Tanzania, Ethiopia) comprised healthy individuals. Historical disease cohorts (CRC, T2D, IBD, etc.) were analyzed from public datasets but not newly sampled.

disease_details.notes: No disease details for newly sequenced healthy cohorts. Disease cohorts from public datasets analyzed but not sample-level disease details provided.

disease_response_recist.notes: No RECIST response criteria data reported.

feces_phenotype.notes: Stool samples collected but no specific phenotypic measurements reported.

fmt_id.notes: No FMT study conducted; this is a microbiome survey study.

fmt_role.notes: Not applicable; no FMT procedure described.

hla.notes: HLA typing not performed or reported.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Birth weight not reported despite inclusion of infants and paired mother-infant samples.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Infant feeding method not reported despite inclusion of 26 infants from Ethiopia.

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: Gestational age at birth not reported.

obgyn_lactating.notes: Lactation status not reported despite inclusion of mothers in Ethiopian cohort.

obgyn_pregnancy.notes: Pregnancy status not reported, though Ethiopian cohort included mothers.

treatment.notes: No treatments or medications reported for the newly sequenced healthy cohorts.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Not applicable; no cancer patients in newly sequenced cohorts.

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: Not applicable; no cancer patients in newly sequenced cohorts.

biomarker_name.notes: The paper does not report clinical biomarkers (e.g., serological markers, hormones). It focuses on microbial genetic/phylogenetic markers and CAZy families for metabolic potential, which are not biomarkers of human disease or health status in the conventional sense.

biomarker_unit.notes: No biomarker units reported; microbial markers are reported as prevalence percentages or presence/absence.

biomarker_value.notes: No conventional biomarker values reported. The paper reports P. copri prevalence (95.4% non-Westernized, 29.6% Westernized) and clade-specific prevalences.

disease_response_os.notes: This is a microbiome population genomics study; no overall survival data are reported.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status is not reported. The study includes healthy individuals from non-Westernized and Westernized populations and disease cohorts (CRC, T2D, IBD, etc.) but does not report individual patient performance status.

feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: prevalence in non-Westernized populations was nearly ubiquitous (95.4% prevalence), in contrast to Westernized populations (29.6% prevalence). Considering each clade separately, all four were significantly more prevalent in non-Westernized compared to westernized datasets
feces_phenotype_value.section: Results — Co-presence of Multiple P. copri Complex Clades
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal phenotype interpreted as P. copri clade prevalence and co-presence patterns in gut microbiome.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: This is a microbiome genomics study; no tumor size measurements are reported.

value: Study analyzed >6,500 metagenomes from 36 datasets across 6 continents and 25 countries
Reconstructed >1,000 P. copri genomes (17 isolates, 1,006 MAGs)
Four distinct clades (A, B, C, D) identified with >10% inter-clade ANI distance
Ancient metagenomes analyzed from 5,300-year-old Iceman and pre-Columbian coprolites
P. copri clade diversification estimated ~6.5 million years ago
Clade B split occurred approximately 6.5 million years ago
Clades A, D, C diversification ~3.5 to ~2.5 million years ago
All four clades were feature of pre-migratory human ancestors
Substantial functional diversity in carbohydrate metabolism repertoires between clades
Clade B enriched for pectin-degrading families PL9 and PL10
Clade D enriched for cellulase family GH9
No significant disease associations found at clade level across meta-analysis
Multi-generational dietary modifications hypothesized as driver of reduced prevalence in Westernized populations
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: P. copri began to diversify (split of clade B) ∼6.5 million years ago. The diversification of clades A, D, and C is estimated to have occurred between ∼3.5 and ∼2.5 million years ago.
uncurated_metadata.section: Results — P. copri Diversity in Ancient Human Gut Contents
uncurated_metadata.notes: Uncurated metadata includes key phylogenetic, functional, and epidemiological findings not fitting other fields.

host_species.evidence_quote: Prevotella copri is a common human gut microbe; human gut microbiome
host_species.notes: Study focused on human gut microbiota. Participants from Ghana, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Madagascar, Peru, Fiji, Mongolia, China, Israel, Mexico, and Europe.

Westernized status set to 'No' based on paper's classification of these cohorts as 'non-Westernized populations'.
Sequencing platform inferred as 'IlluminaHiSeq' from Methods: 'sequenced on the Illumina HiSeq2500 100nt paired end platform'.
No individual subject_id or sample_id values reported; sample rows represent demographic aggregates from each cohort.
Sex reported only as percentages in Methods (Ghana 52.2% female, Ethiopia 100% female, Tanzania 48.65% female); sample rows represent single-sex groups derived from these percentages.

This study is primarily a metagenomic survey and population genetics study of P. copri microbiota across global populations. Newly sequenced cohorts (Ghana, Tanzania, Ethiopia with 162 individuals total) were healthy and lacked detailed clinical phenotype information. Historical disease association analyses were conducted on public datasets (CRC, T2D, IBD, hypertension, liver cirrhosis) but individual-level disease data was not provided in the main text. The schema fields are primarily designed for clinical studies with detailed participant phenotyping, which is not the focus of this microbiome study.
Ancient human samples (Iceman mummy and pre-Columbian coprolites) were analyzed but are not appropriate for the clinical participant schema fields.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

This is a microbiome population genomics study, not a clinical trial or biomarker study. Most conventional biomarker fields (disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, tumor_size) are not applicable.
The study analyzes P. copri genetic and population structure across geographic and lifestyle contexts (Westernized vs non-Westernized) rather than individual patient clinical outcomes.
No individual patient-level data are provided in tables; analysis is at the cohort/dataset level.
Disease associations with P. copri clades were investigated but no strong associations were found across the meta-analysis.
Ancient metagenome samples (Iceman, Mexican coprolites) are included but represent archaeological specimens, not living study participants.
